title: Conversation Mining
lead: Normalizing AI chat transcripts and filing them verbatim, message by message.
summary: MemPalace converts diverse chat export formats (Claude Code JSONL, ChatGPT, Gemini CLI, OpenAI Codex, Slack, Claude.ai JSON) into a normalized transcript via the --mode convos pipeline. The primary miner chunks by exchange pair (Q+A) or extracts memory types, while the sweeper catches per-message outliers missed by file-level chunking. Diary ingest files daily summaries atomically per day with incremental change detection.

concepts.definition: One user turn (prefixed >) plus the AI response that follows; the primary chunking unit in conversation mining, preserving Q+A semantics rather than arbitrary character boundaries.

Chunking strategy: 'exchange' (default) preserves conversation structure, while 'general' applies heuristic keyword matching to extract 5 memory types (decisions, preferences, milestones, problems, emotional) with per-chunk classification.
Format auto-detection and conversion of diverse chat export schemas (7+ formats) to a canonical >-prefixed transcript format with noise stripping and tool-result truncation.
Timestamp-coordinated, idempotent message-level ingestion that catches individual messages missed by file-level chunking; uses a cursor and deterministic IDs to resume cleanly after crashes.
Schema versioning constant (v2) that gates incremental ingest and triggers auto-purge of pre-v2 drawers on schema bumps, preventing mixed old/new rows in the same source.
Heuristic routing that auto-defaults conversation files from .claude/projects, .codex, or .gemini to wing_api, with fallback to dirname-based slugification for other sources.
Atomic grouping of diary topics into fixed-character closets (indexed summaries) that never split mid-topic, with full rebuild on content changes to prevent orphaned closets.
Per-(palace, diary-dir) state file tracking content hash and entry count to skip unchanged diary files and detect in-place edits without re-ingesting entire days.
Pluggable ingestion contract (BaseSourceAdapter) for third-party sources (Cursor, GitHub, Slack APIs) with declared transformations, metadata schema, and privacy class.

symbols.name: mine_convos
symbols.role: Entry point for file-level conversation mining; acquires palace lock, calls _mine_convos_impl with ingest mode ('exchange' or 'general').

symbols.name: normalize
symbols.role: Auto-detects chat export format and normalizes to >-prefixed transcript; dispatches to format-specific parsers.

symbols.name: chunk_exchanges
symbols.role: Primary chunking strategy: groups user turns (>) with AI responses as one drawer, falls back to paragraph/line-group chunking.

symbols.name: sweep
symbols.role: Message-level secondary ingestion path; uses cursor + deterministic IDs for idempotent, resume-safe per-message mining.

symbols.name: ingest_diaries
symbols.role: Ingest daily summaries with incremental change detection; splits by ## headers, packs closets, purges stale closets on rebuild.

symbols.name: BaseSourceAdapter
symbols.role: Abstract contract for RFC 002 source adapters; defines ingest(), describe_schema(), is_current(), and transformation declarations.

symbols.name: get_adapter
symbols.role: Returns cached adapter instance; discovers entry points on first call and caches instances per adapter name.

symbols.name: strip_noise
symbols.role: Removes Claude Code system tags, hook output, and UI chrome using line-anchored patterns that refuse to cross blank lines.

symbols.name: prefetch_mined_set
symbols.role: Single paginated scan to collect all source_files at current NORMALIZE_VERSION, enabling O(1) skip checks.

symbols.name: PalaceContext
symbols.role: Facade passed to adapters; bundles drawer/closet collections, knowledge graph, palace config, and progress hooks; shields adapters from direct palace imports.

surprises.title: Tie-Break Safety: < Cursor, Not <= Cursor
surprises.detail: The sweep uses < cursor (strictly earlier) instead of <= cursor. When multiple messages share the same ISO-8601 timestamp and only some were ingested before a crash, a <= skip would lose the rest forever. The < skip allows deterministic drawer IDs to deduplicate at the cursor boundary on re-run, making resumption safe.

surprises.title: Slack Multi-Party Speakers: Role Alternation
surprises.detail: Slack exports have no inherent 'user' or 'assistant'. The parser assigns alternating roles to different speaker IDs, prefixing each message with the speaker ID so downstream chunking (which relies on > markers) still works. A provenance footer marks the transcript as Slack-imported so consumers know speaker roles are positional, not verified.

surprises.title: Memory Type Metadata: Per-Chunk Classification
surprises.detail: In 'general' extract_mode, chunks from general_extractor carry a per-chunk memory_type (decision/preference/milestone/problem/emotional). Rather than using a file-level room, each chunk's memory_type becomes its drawer room. Room count deltas are accumulated per chunk, not per file, allowing fine-grained room stats.

surprises.title: Stale Drawer Purge: Pre-v2 Rows Don't Coexist with v2
surprises.detail: When normalize_version increments (v1 to v2), _source_file_delete_ids filters by extract_mode and removes all pre-v2 drawers for the source before upserting fresh chunks. This prevents mixed schema rows and ensures schema bumps apply uniformly. Legacy drawers without extract_mode metadata are treated as 'exchange' mode for cleanup.

surprises.title: Diary Full Rebuild on In-Place Edits
surprises.detail: If content_hash changes but entry_count stays the same (e.g., editing a sentence within an entry), full_rebuild is triggered. This catches content re-ordering and in-place changes that would otherwise leave stale closets. The purge-before-insert pattern ensures orphaned closets from prior runs don't survive.

designDecisions.decision: Exchange Pair as Chunking Unit (Not Fixed Char Size)
designDecisions.rationale: Preserving Q+A semantics makes search results more coherent - a user's question and the AI's answer stay together in one drawer, enabling exchange-level search and retrieval. Fixed-char chunking (as used in project mining) would split exchange pairs arbitrarily, losing context. The fallback to paragraph-then-line-group chunking accommodates content without quote markers.

designDecisions.decision: Extract Mode as Dual-Path (Exchange vs. General Memory Types)
designDecisions.rationale: Exchange mode serves conversation-as-conversation use cases; general mode supports decision/preference/problem tracking for non-conversational summaries (meeting notes, journaling). By making it a per-ingest flag (not a runtime toggle), each source gets consistent room classification, and the state file gates incremental re-runs per mode.

designDecisions.decision: Per-Message Sweep as Secondary Path, Not Primary
designDecisions.rationale: The sweeper catches edge cases (individual messages that fall between file-level chunk boundaries) without introducing complexity into the primary miner. Separation of concerns keeps the file miner fast and simple while allowing the sweep to run independently on JSONL sources. Coordination happens via idempotent drawer IDs, not shared state.

designDecisions.decision: Wing Auto-Detection from Path, Fallback to Dirname
designDecisions.rationale: Claude Code / Codex / Gemini conversations are API-sourced and should group under wing_api by default (not per-project). User-provided --wing always wins. For non-AI-tool sources, the dirname basename is more useful than a generic API label. The _resolve_wing function centralizes this logic with fallback ordering.

designDecisions.decision: Diary State File in ~/.mempalace/state/, Not User's Diary Dir
designDecisions.rationale: State files should not live in user content directories (avoid clutter and accidental edits). Keying by sha256(palace_path|diary_dir) allows multiple diary folders to share one palace without conflicts. The state file enables incremental ingest and in-place edit detection without re-hashing unchanged content every run.

related.why: Explains how conversation mining fits into the broader MemPalace ingest -> search -> retrieve pipeline and the role of the palace model (wings/rooms/drawers/closets).
Details the drawer/closet/hall structure that conversation mining populates; critical for understanding how room detection and hall routing work.
Entity extraction from conversation content is used to tag drawer metadata for filterable search; diary ingest also stamps entities on daily summaries.
Closets created by diary ingest use the AAAK dialect for indexed summaries; related to how multi-topic packing avoids splitting mid-topic.
Search queries return conversation drawers; understanding how room, hall, and entity metadata filter results clarifies why normalization includes room/hall detection.
Drawer and closet collections use RFC 001 backend abstraction (Chroma, SQLite, etc.); conversation mining is format-agnostic across backends.

searchDoc.title: Conversation Mining
searchDoc.summary: MemPalace converts diverse chat export formats (Claude Code JSONL, ChatGPT, Gemini CLI, OpenAI Codex, Slack, Claude.ai JSON) into a normalized >-prefixed transcript via the --mode convos pipeline. The primary miner chunks by exchange pair or extracts memory types, the sweeper catches per-message outliers, and diary ingest files daily summaries with incremental change detection.
searchDoc.body: Conversation mining is a multi-path ingestion pipeline that turns AI chat transcripts into searchable drawers in the MemPalace. Files enter through scan_convos, where the normalize function auto-detects the export format from extension and content shape, then dispatches to format-specific parsers for Claude Code JSONL, ChatGPT mapping trees, Gemini CLI, OpenAI Codex, Slack JSON exports, and Claude.ai JSON. Each parser extracts (role, text) message pairs and converts them to a canonical greater-than-prefixed transcript. The strip_noise function removes Claude Code system tags, hook output, and UI chrome using patterns anchored to line boundaries that refuse to cross blank lines, preventing a stray tag in one message from eating content in adjacent messages. Tool results are truncated per message: Bash output uses head and tail windows, Grep and Glob cap at twenty matches, and Read, Edit, and Write results are omitted entirely. After normalization, chunk_exchanges groups each user turn with the AI response that follows as one drawer, preserving question and answer semantics rather than splitting at arbitrary character boundaries. If fewer than three quote markers are found it falls back to paragraph then line-group chunking. General extract mode instead pulls five memory types: decisions, preferences, milestones, problems, and emotional. Each chunk gets a room via keyword scoring and a hall via cached config keywords, and a deterministic drawer ID derived from source file, extract mode, and chunk index. When NORMALIZE_VERSION bumps, prefetch_mined_set scans the palace once to collect already-mined files, turning O(n) per-file queries into one paginated pass that saves about an hour on large palaces. Pre-v2 drawers are purged before fresh chunks upsert so schema versions never mix. A secondary sweeper processes Claude Code JSONL message by message, using a timestamp cursor and deterministic IDs keyed by session and message uuid for idempotent, resume-safe ingestion; it uses strictly-less-than cursor comparison so siblings sharing a timestamp are not lost after a crash. Diary ingest splits daily summary files on double-hash headers, hashes content with SHA-256 to detect changes, and packs entries into closets in the AAAK dialect without splitting mid-topic. RFC 002 source adapters declare transformations and register via setuptools entry points, invoked through a PalaceContext facade.
